controlled_change: 1072 versus 1460 CLOCK slots; both use core-cache residency, immediate execution and the same 12GiB maximum. Two fresh alternating pairs on the unchanged native build and mixed artifact.
correctness: All output tokens, actual history reuse and arithmetic dispatch counts match. Same-build prior full-model state and forced-eviction evidence was revalidated. No new state qualification at 1460 slots.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: At least 20ms per token saved in both decode phases, with improved complete conversations and unchanged first-token guards.
hypothesis: An extra 1GiB of expert slots under core-cache residency avoids enough required reads to materially reduce decode latency.
limitations: Two short pairs establish a directional screen, not confidence bounds or 2K/4K performance.
Phase-boundary memory observations are not continuous monitoring or a sustained-use qualification.
Historical routing simulations omit native leases and overlap; read reductions are not latency predictions.
outcome: All four processes were clean. Median paired conversation latency fell 1.77%; initial/append throughput medians were 4.106/3.689 versus 4.371/3.870 tokens/s. Savings of 14.78/12.65ms per token miss the fixed stage target. No five-pair confirmation or production promotion.
smallest_experiment: Stop capacity growth and keep 1072 slots as the reference. Use the completed clean resident-decode trace to isolate a larger source of serial work before routing.
